notify.payloadEnvelopeHint: A fixed JSON object carrying the event, the subject and the rendered text.
notify.payloadTemplateHint: The message template below becomes the whole request body. Use this for Slack, Teams or Alertmanager, which each want their own shape.
notify.tplJsonNote: This body IS the request payload, so it must be valid JSON. Values you insert are escaped for you; the quotes and commas around them are yours.
notify.deliveriesHint: What was sent, what is waiting, and what was given up on. A given-up delivery is the only record that an alert never arrived.
notify.bodyFormatHint: Chooses the Content-Type header, how substituted values are escaped, and what the body is checked against before it is sent. There is no YAML: whether a value needs quoting there depends on its content and its indentation, and getting it subtly wrong produces a document that parses as something else.
notify.emailFormatHint: HTML sends one text/html part and escapes substituted values as HTML. There is no plain-text alternative part: it would have to be guessed from your markup.
notify.syslogDetailHint: Structured data carries the event id, category, severity and source, which is how a collector deduplicates retries. Some collectors log the whole line as text, where it is noise in front of the message.
notify.previewSyslog: The line that will be sent
notify.previewEmail: The message that will be sent
notify.previewContentType: The Content-Type header this request will carry
notify.previewSyslogNoSubject: Syslog carries no subject; only the body is sent.

preset.title: Dashboard presets
preset.intro: A preset is a file describing what to poll on one kind of equipment and how to show it. Adding one here does not start anything: it is bound when you add a target.

preset.costNotAPrediction: These are counts, not a duration: how long a round takes depends on the device and the link. If a round stops fitting inside the cadence, the poll clock widens it and says so.

windows-server.name: Windows server
windows-server.description: A Windows Server 2022 host with its SNMP service: adapters and Windows’s pseudo-interfaces, addresses, routes and sockets (RDP, SMB, IIS), drives by letter, processes and installed programs. Fits the “Interfaces (IF-MIB)” and “Server (HOST-RESOURCES-MIB)” presets.

cisco-catalyst-24.name: Cisco Catalyst 2960, 24 ports
cisco-catalyst-24.description: An access switch: 24 Fast Ethernet ports, two gigabit uplinks and VLAN 1, with its MAC address table, spanning tree, VLANs (Q-BRIDGE and VTP), LLDP and CDP neighbours, ENTITY-MIB hardware, and Cisco’s CPU, memory and environment. Recognised as a Cisco, so the “Cisco (IF-MIB)” preset comes first; also fits “Switch ports” and “Switch drawing (24 ports)”.

cisco-catalyst-48.name: Cisco Catalyst 2960, 48 ports
cisco-catalyst-48.description: The same access switch with 48 ports, and everything that goes with them. Recognised as a Cisco, so the “Cisco (IF-MIB)” preset comes first; also fits “Switch ports”.

cisco-isr-4331.name: Cisco ISR 4331 router
cisco-isr-4331.description: A branch router: WAN, LAN and management ports, two eBGP sessions — one established, one not — and the routes the first brought, its ARP cache and sockets, ENTITY-MIB hardware, and Cisco’s CPU, memory and environment. Sends the BGP notifications and configuration changes.

synology-nas.name: Synology NAS
synology-nas.description: A DS920+ on DSM: Synology’s system, disk and RAID tables beside interfaces, a file server’s sockets (SMB, AFP, NFS), host resources with processes and packages, and UCD-SNMP-MIB. Fits the “Interfaces (IF-MIB)” and “Server (HOST-RESOURCES-MIB)” presets.

apc-smart-ups.name: APC Smart-UPS, three-phase
apc-smart-ups.description: A 10 kVA UPS on its network card, answering the standard UPS-MIB — battery, input and output per phase — and APC’s PowerNet-MIB alike, from the same readings. Fits the “UPS (RFC 1628)” preset and sends upsTrapOnBattery.

hp-laserjet.name: HP LaserJet printer
hp-laserjet.description: A network laser printer answering the Printer MIB: trays, output bin, cover, marker and page counts, a black cartridge running low and its alert, the languages it reads and its panel, with the printer in the host resources. Sends printerV2Alert.

environment-probe.name: Environment probe
environment-probe.description: A temperature and humidity probe answering the standard ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB, as a server room’s cold aisle reads, with its hardware in ENTITY-MIB.

linux-server.name: Linux server
linux-server.description: An Ubuntu 24.04 host running net-snmp, as a walk of one finds it: interfaces, addresses, routes and sockets; its devices, file systems, processes and packages; UCD-SNMP-MIB’s memory, load and disks. Fits the “Interfaces (IF-MIB)” and “Server (HOST-RESOURCES-MIB)” presets.

dell-idrac9.name: Dell iDRAC9 (PowerEdge R750)
dell-idrac9.description: The out-of-band controller of a PowerEdge R750 (IDRAC-MIB): global, storage and power status, BIOS, processors, memory modules, power supplies, temperatures, fans, consumption, and the RAID controller with its physical and virtual disks. Sends alertTemperatureProbeWarning.

mikrotik-rb4011.name: MikroTik RB4011 router
mikrotik-rb4011.description: A RouterOS router for a small office: ten gigabit ports and an empty SFP+ cage, a LAN bridge on 192.168.88.0/24, its routes and services, the board’s health (MIKROTIK-MIB), the neighbours MNDP and LLDP found, and host resources. Fits the “Interfaces (IF-MIB)” and “Server (HOST-RESOURCES-MIB)” presets.

fortigate-60f.name: Fortinet FortiGate 60F
fortigate-60f.description: A branch firewall on FortiOS 7.2: two WAN ports — the backup one down —, DMZ, LAN and the SSL VPN tunnel, its routes, and FortiGate’s processor, memory, disk, sessions, VDOM, HA mode, policy counters and IPsec tunnels. Sends the processor and memory threshold notifications.

unifi-u6-pro.name: UniFi U6 Pro access point
unifi-u6-pro.description: A Wi-Fi 6 access point: two radios and how busy their channels are, three SSIDs with their clients, traffic, errors and retries (UBNT-UniFi-MIB), its LLDP neighbour, host resources and UCD-SNMP-MIB.

apc-rack-pdu.name: APC switched rack PDU
apc-rack-pdu.description: An AP7921B: eight outlets, one of them switched off, the phase load in amps and the power drawn (PowerNet-MIB), beside the card’s address and services. Sends rPDUOutletOff and rPDUNearOverload.

simulator.firstUserTarget: Add as target uses the first user who can write, or else the first.

traps.hint: Where the device sends its traps and INFORMs, and when. Unlike where it answers, a destination may be anywhere on the network.
traps.engineIdHint: SnmpLens cannot be discovered: to send it an INFORM, give its engine ID.
traps.newDestinationNote: A new destination is SnmpLens on this machine, at its trap port.
traps.onStart: Send coldStart when the device starts
traps.onAuthFailure: Send authenticationFailure when a request is refused (about once a second at most)
traps.sendTitle: Send one of the device's notifications to its destinations now
traps.sentAll: {name} sent to {count, plural, one {# destination} other {# destinations}}
traps.activity: {sent, plural, one {# notification sent} other {# notifications sent}}

picker.importTitle: Add models from a JSON file, or from a ZIP holding their icons or whole packages with recorded walks
picker.recordTitle: Walk a real device and keep what it answers as a model
picker.exportModel: Export this model as a package (ZIP), to edit or share it
picker.inUse: {count, plural, one {# device is made from this model: delete it first} other {# devices are made from this model: delete them first}}

record.hint: SnmpLens walks the device with the identifiers its target uses and keeps every value it answers, as a package — its SNMP users, groups and communities excepted. A large device takes a while.
record.name: Model name
record.progress: {count, plural, one {# object recorded…} other {# objects recorded…}}
record.stopped: The recording was stopped; nothing was kept.

models.replaced: Model “{name}” updated; the devices running it have restarted

warning.iconSkipped: {name}: its icon “{detail}” was not imported — an icon travels in a ZIP, beside its model
warning.iconMissing: {name}: the archive holds no “{detail}”, so the model has no icon
warning.walkSkipped: {name}: recorded values that could not be read were left out ({detail})
warning.walkAgentOwned: {name}: {detail} recorded objects belong to the agent itself — its SNMP counters, engine, users, groups and communities — and were left out
warning.packageIgnored: {name}: “{detail}” is not a file a package reads, and was left out
